prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the pii-chat agent (card support: identity checks, lost and stolen cards, replacements) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: hearing loss and phone calls. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member mentions hearing loss or that they struggle on the phone, slow the pace, speak one point at a time, and check understanding before moving on."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a call quality issue makes identity checks difficult, offer to repeat key security questions clearly and avoid rushing through verification."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member prefers not to rely on spoken instructions, I should offer to summarise the next steps in simple language and confirm the safest way to continue."},{"type":"observation","content":"When background noise or audio distortion is affecting the call, I should keep questions short and use plain wording so the member can follow more easily."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a member cannot clearly hear the card loss or replacement options, I should restate the choices calmly and make sure they know which action will happen next."},{"type":"preference","content":"When someone says phone calls are difficult, I should be patient and let them answer in their own time rather than filling the silence too quickly."},{"type":"observation","content":"When hearing loss is mentioned, I should avoid speaking over the member and wait for a natural pause before asking the next security or card-support question."},{"type":"fact","content":"When confirming a lost or stolen card, it helps to recap the outcome at the end of the call in one clear sentence so there is no confusion."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member seems unsure because they missed part of the call, I should invite them to ask me to repeat anything rather than assuming they have understood."},{"type":"observation","content":"When communication is harder by voice, I should keep the process structured, signpost each stage, and make the replacement card steps feel predictable."}]}
